page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Actinomorphic
lines: Actinomorphic flower: it can be cut into two
equal halves in ANY vertical plane passing
steps.why: The test is the cutting plane: ANY vertical plane gives equal halves - that is radial symmetry.
common_mistakes: Leaving out 'any plane'. Without it the two definitions read the same.
steps.memory_tip: Actino - like rays of a wheel: cut anywhere through the centre, the halves match.
steps.margin_note: The word ANY plus one example carries the mark.

steps.label: Zygomorphic

lines.text: Zygomorphic flower: it can be cut into two

lines: equal halves in only ONE vertical plane
steps.why: Same test, opposite result: only ONE plane works - bilateral symmetry, as in the pea flower.
common_mistakes: Swapping the examples: Hibiscus and mustard are actinomorphic; pea and bean are zygomorphic.
steps.memory_tip: Zygo - only one plane, like a face: one line of symmetry only.
steps.margin_note: ANY versus ONE is the whole table - underline both words.
